title: The big lookout: year one close
hookLine: stories, practices, the Psalms and Mark, the mystics, the Catechism: a whole landscape seen from here
tomorrow: year two opens: a library, not a book

lines: HEAD DOWN, ONE SWITCHBACK AT A TIME.
A BENCH AT THE TOP OF YEAR ONE.
cards: An hour into the trail, it's all roots and rocks, head down, one switchback after another. You stop noticing how high you've come. Then the trees open: a rail, a bench, and the whole valley below you.
The river you crossed at the start, the ridge you thought would never end, the parking lot, tiny now. Three hundred thirty-one days, and a bench at the top of year one. Sit down.

teach.b: Camp one was first words: grace, the sign of the cross, the Mass, Mary, the saints, the rosary, confession, Sunday, the Our Father, Lent, Easter, the Eucharist, mercy, the Psalms.
Camp two, the stories: the child, the parables, Holy Week, the cross and the morning, the fire of Pentecost, the saints one by one.
Camp three, the practices: the body at prayer, the Mass scene by scene, the rosary, the seven sacraments, confession up close, adoration, the Church's year.

teach.h: THE PSALMS, THEN MARK STRAIGHT THROUGH.
teach.b: Then the text: the Psalms, whose words Jesus cries out from the cross in Mark, then Mark straight through, ending at an empty tomb and a young man saying he goes before you.
Then the depths, ways of praying: lectio divina, the examen, the Jesus Prayer, a friar at his pots and pans. Teresa's crystal castle with God at the center. John of the Cross and his dark night.
Thomas Merton on a Louisville street corner.
Then the Catechism, a map and not a wall, all the way to sursum corda. The Bible has a lookout too.

teach.h: MOSES SEES THE WHOLE LAND FROM NEBO.
teach.b: At the end of Deuteronomy, Moses climbs Mount Nebo, and God shows him the whole land at once: Gilead as far as Dan, Naphtali, Ephraim and Manasseh, Judah to the far sea, the plain of Jericho, the city of palm trees.
The text is honest: he sees it with his eyes, but doesn't cross over. Others will walk it. A lookout isn't the end of the walking.
It's where you finally see what you've been walking through.
Catholics answer at Mass, after the readings and at the very end: thanks be to God, in Latin Deo gratias.

how: At Mass, Catholics answer "Thanks be to God" (Deo gratias) after the first readings and at the dismissal, and some parishes sing the Te Deum, an ancient hymn of thanksgiving, on the last day of the calendar year.

o: God be with you, a greeting at the start of Mass
praise to God, sung only on the great feast days
thanks be to God, the people's answer at Mass

games.q: what's inside the year — tap the pairs.
p: where Moses saw the whole land

s: in Deuteronomy, Moses crosses into the land he sees from Mount Nebo
he sees it all with his eyes, but the text says he doesn't cross over. others will walk it.
at Mass, Catholics answer thanks be to God after the readings
and again at the very end. in Latin, deo gratias.
year one ended with the Gospel of Mark
Mark closed camp four. camp five went into the depths: the mystics, then the Catechism.

games.q: you're Moses, old now, at the top of Mount Nebo. God shows you the whole land at once, from Gilead to the city of palm trees. what happens?
o: you walk down and cross over into it.
you see all of it with your eyes, and don't cross over.
you turn your back and look at the desert behind you.
games.why: he sees it with his eyes, and the text is honest: he doesn't cross over. others will walk it. the lookout shows the whole land at once.

practice: Let the year come back, not in order: a word that stuck, a story you told someone, a day you almost skipped and didn't, a day you skipped and came back anyway. Don't grade it; just say thanks for each thing that comes.
If you pray, use the old words from the Mass, thanks be to God; if you don't, a plain thank you is enough.

wordCard.voice: Deo gratias, the people's answer at Mass, thanks be to God: the view from the bench at the end of year one. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: thanks be to God, the people's answer at Mass after the readings and at the dismissal.

carryVoice: Your line: you know this country now. Tomorrow the trail goes on: year two opens the Bible itself, in order. See you there.
